subject: general
question: According to the office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, a city with a population exceeding 10 million is classified as which type of urban settlement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mega City**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A city with a population exceeding 10 million is classified as a **Mega City** according to the office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.
 
• Mega Cities are large urban areas with high population density and significant economic, social, and political influence.
 
• Examples of Mega Cities in India include **Delhi**, **Mumbai**, and **Kolkata**, as per recent census data.
 
• The term "Mega City" is used globally to categorize urban settlements with populations exceeding 10 million, aligning with United Nations standards.
 
• The classification helps in urban planning, resource allocation, and policy-making to address challenges like infrastructure, housing, and transportation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban Settlements Classification**:

 
 
• Urban settlements are classified based on population size, density, and administrative importance.
 
• Categories include towns, cities, metropolitan cities, and mega cities.
 
• A Metropolitan City typically has a population between 1 million to 10 million.
 
 
 
• **Global Mega Cities**:
 
 
• Some of the world's largest Mega Cities include Tokyo, Shanghai, and São Paulo.
 
• These cities serve as hubs for finance, culture, and international trade.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Mega Cities**:
 
 
• Mega Cities often face issues such as overcrowding, pollution, inadequate infrastructure, and housing shortages.
 
• Governments implement policies to improve urban management and sustainability.
 
 
 
• **India's Census Data**:
 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years to collect demographic, social, and economic data.
 
• The classification of urban settlements is based on this data to ensure effective governance.
